newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile oil firm Enap eyes natgas pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: Chile oil firm Enap eyes natgas pipeline project.

text.p: Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (Enap) said it is studying buying British and U.S investors' stakes in the ill-fated TransGas pipeline project which was to bring natural gas to Chile from Argentina.
Enap is a small shareholder in the project which was to be built by British Gas and Tenneco TGT.N.
The scheme has lain dormant after losing the battle in 1995 against the rival Gas Andes pipeline group to supply Santiago with natural gas.

"The board has authorized us to negotiate a possible offer to our partners in the project and at the minute we are in talks which could end in the short term," general manager Alvaro Garcia told a news conference.
Garcia declined to give details of the sum under discussion, but said it would be small.
Enap, which operates gas pipelines in Chile's far south, is keen to revive the stretch of the project from Neuquen gas fields in southern Argentina to the Chilean port of Concepcion.
"The project is good from the point of view of the country and we would like to maintain it to develop when it is convenient," said Garcia.

The original Transgas scheme was much longer with the group planning to bring gas from Neuquen directly to Santiago. But it was beaten by the shorter GasAndes pipeline which crosses the Andes from the central Argentine city of Mendoza.
